@graph.name: smart-guideline-end-to-end
@graph.title: smart-guideline-end-to-end

@graph.name: DIIG — from a health system bottleneck to a costed implementation plan
@graph.summary: The nine-chapter sequence of the WHO/ITU Digital Implementation Investment Guide, as the Guide numbers it.
@graph.description:
The nine-chapter sequence of the WHO/ITU Digital Implementation Investment Guide, as the Guide numbers it. Each chapter's output is the next chapter's input, and the two exclusive gateways are the Guide's OWN progress checks (4.5 and 8.5) rather than gates added here.

Adopted whole per `methodology-adoption`, and rendered from the ingested sections at `who-iris/library/9789240010567-eng/`. Chapter 1 is the Guide's introduction — scope, key terms and when the Guide applies — so it is the start event's documentation rather than an activity: nothing is performed there.

ADVISORY, not strict. This is a per-methodology process and DIIG is somebody else's method: the engine can report where a programme has got to, but what counts as an adequate answer to "have we identified the bottlenecks" belongs to the programme and its stakeholders, not to this repository. The four unrelaxable steps of the base editorial gate are untouched by it.

WHAT THIS DIAGRAM DOES NOT DO. DIIG Table 3.3.1 scores bottlenecks on three 1-3 criteria and sums them into a ranking. The three criteria are adopted; the arithmetic is refused, per `methodology-adoption` — three ordinal judgements on incommensurable scales, summed with equal weight, produce a number whose precision is invented. So A_PrioritizeBottlenecks records each criterion's answer and its reason and orders by argument. There is no computed score anywhere in this process, and a DMN-backed gateway would be the wrong shape for exactly that reason.

@graph.description:
Produces a WHO Digital Transformation Handbook (DTH) from its sources to publication, in seven stages that each end in a recorded milestone: initiate (M0 charter), ingest sources into the library (M1 library frozen), outline and scope (M2 outline agreed), structured drafting (M3 zero draft), working-group feedback (M4), public comment (M5 released, M6 dispositioned), and finalise and publish (M7).
Milestones are recorded checkpoints, not gates: each is written as a note on the handbook's epic bean (which milestone, when, evidence), so the site can show stage and progress. Review runs beside drafting as QA, as in smart-guideline-end-to-end.bpmn.
Structured drafting uses the smart-base DAK block kinds for personas, scenarios, processes, decisions, data elements, indicators and requirements, and each track calls Process_L2ComponentEditReview, as l2-dak-authoring.bpmn does. Contributor feedback from the contributor log sheet and from GitHub pc: comments lands in one review store.
Handbooks ingested from a published WHO PDF (PHC, SC, PC, SFP) enter at stage 1 with their library built and their outline given by the publication; dth-hrh, authored natively, is the pilot. Steps with no platform subprocess are marked as placeholders in their documentation.
Empirical content (figures, statistics, country examples) stays as cited narrative blocks and never enters formal content.

typologies
@graph.summary: The graph typologies a harness declares it owns, one node per kind, so no central registry names another harness's subgraph types. Loaded across the instances on first use.

@graph.name: validators
@graph.summary: The validators a harness's code provides, one node each naming the graph typology and $schema family it checks and the Zod export that checks it, joined onto the kinds on first use.

@graph.name: qa-checkers
@graph.summary: The QA checkers a harness provides, one node per criterion naming the table that holds the code; registered for a folio through its dependency tree.

@graph.name: block-kinds
@graph.summary: The block kinds a harness's adapter owns, one node per kind carrying its label prefix, RDF types, profile and builder. Discovered across the instances; no module lists them.

@graph.name: content-adapters
@graph.summary: The block vocabularies a harness owns, one node per vocabulary carrying its companion roles and whether the platform's code types it. Discovered across the instances; no module lists them.

@graph.name: tools
@graph.summary: Tool definitions — themselves nodes in the KG, per the repo taxonomy.

@graph.name: skills
@graph.summary: A Subgraph of Skills: the instructions an Actor follows to carry out a Task.

@graph.name: processes
@graph.summary: A Subgraph of Processes: BPMN diagrams that coordinate Tasks, and the decision tables their gateways compute from.

@graph.name: scenarios
@graph.summary: A Subgraph of Roles: the responsibilities an Actor takes on, and who takes them on.

@graph.name: methodology
@graph.summary: Judgement methodologies, adopted whole and kept independent — parallel ways to reach a decision, selected by context.

@graph.name: docs
@graph.summary: Documentation ABOUT the knowledge graph — how the harness works, what its directories hold, how a process runs. Rendered by the plain just-the-docs pipeline. Distinct from `folio`, which is content an author CREATES using the graph; the difference is the SUBJECT, not the format. An L1 library's catalogue is `library/`; a note about it is a `folio`; the page explaining how ingestion works is `docs`.

@graph.name: code-list
@graph.summary: Closed sets of codes — adjudication answers, the namespaces this project mints — one file per list, every code carrying its definition and source, published as SKOS.

@graph.name: schemas
@graph.summary: A Subgraph of Node Schemas: files that state the shape other files must have.

@graph.name: qa
@graph.summary: QA verdicts and their projections — kg-qa audits, block and translation QA, qa-witness documents for the docs site, the viewer-navbar audit, result roll-ups and test runs; every `$schema` family is named in `nodeSchemas`, which is the list — a count here would be a second one, and it was already wrong by one before `viewer-nav-qa/v1` was added. Generated; never hand-edited.

@graph.name: code
@graph.summary: Source code -- the modules, scripts and entry points an instance holds. Declared so that code is scannable at all: an undeclared file is one no checker has a reason to look at. Being declared here says nothing about whether a Tool node claims it, which is a separate question and a separate axis.

@graph.name: library
@graph.summary: L1 source content — one `<bib-slug>/` per ingested document, holding `sections/*.md`, `structure.json` and, where the source was scanned, `ocr/page-NNN.txt`. Every knowledge-graph reference to a source resolves through here, never to a loose path or a bare URL.

@graph.name: voices
@graph.summary: Editorial voice profiles — one JSON each, carrying `"$schema": "folio-voice/v1"`. Every rule cites the ingested source or KG node it was derived from. Opt-in per folio.

@graph.name: themes
@graph.summary: Themes derived from an instance's own sources — one Theme node each, carrying `kind: sticky | webpage | publication`. The palette vocabulary is shared across every kind and only the geometry varies; every value cites where it was measured.

@graph.name: document-kinds
@graph.summary: Document kinds — named structures of sections (fixed or semi-fixed) that a document authored with a harness follows, one `document-kind/1.0.0` JSON each, plus computed `document-kind-coverage/1.0.0` reports of how a subject realises one. Every kind and section names its sources; `computedFrom` names the declared graphs a section derives from.

@graph.name: translation-sources
@graph.summary: POT templates, PO catalogues and their `TranslationNode` manifests, one directory per target locale. The INPUT to injection; the rendered output is ordinary content that declares its own `lang`.

@graph.name: fhir-artifact-index
@graph.summary: The artefact index of a published FHIR Implementation Guide, reconstructed from its published output — every artefact by canonical URL and published representation, with the IG API's JSON Schema / JSON-LD sidecars as an overlay where the IG publishes them. No IG publishes such an index itself, so every field records which file it came out of.

@graph.name: ig-pages
@graph.summary: The pages of a FHIR Implementation Guide mirror, generated from its artefact index and the chrome of its template chain. Carried beside `docs` on the same directory: `docs` is how the site mounts them, and this kind is what says they are derived.

@graph.name: glossary
@graph.summary: SKOS terms (folio-glossary/v1): local terms with definitions and codes, linked to external SKOS schemes by exactMatch rather than copied. Rendered on the glossary/ page.

@graph.name: l1-extraction
@graph.summary: What the recommendation-extraction skill read out of ONE library entry, held beside it at `library/<entry>/l1-extraction/` when the same instance holds the entry, or at `l1-extractions/<entry>/` when the entry lives in another instance (smart-base's handbook extraction, whose source moved to who-iris on 2026-10-30, who-iris#107): the L1 A-Box graph (`l1.json`, JSON-LD against the WHO SMART L1 ontology), the L2 scenario candidates derived from it (`scenarios/scenario-candidates.l2.json`), and the curation, vocabulary and run context that produced them. A sub-graph of `library`: nested in an entry, it is published with the entry beside the entry's manifest; held apart, its own viewer (`scripts/gen-l1-extraction-pages.ts`) publishes it. It is never a folder named for an entry another library holds, which reads as a second copy of that entry and makes the library ingest refuse the duplicate slug.

@graph.title: L1 extraction reviewer
@graph.description: Signs, or rejects, the exclusions an L1 extraction proposes: each normative-looking sentence of a WHO publication that the curation says is not a recommendation, an implementation practice or a remark. Until a person acting in this role signs an exclusion, its sentence stays unaccounted and coverage stays below 100 %. Owner ruling 3b, 2026-10-12: exclusions are signed by this named role, never by the agent that proposed them. Inherits the harness's generic reviewer and performs exclusion sign-off in `classify-and-code-content.bpmn` (bean 4nfs).

@graph.name: smart-base-site-docs
@graph.description: This instance's pages for the platform's docs site: the WHO SMART DAK and IG authoring guides and the WHO SMART content types. Composed through just-the-docs (`composed: true`), so its pages land in the platform's site under this instance's name. `docs.json` declares `source/`, which the platform's docs-page run renders, one `source/<group>-<slug>/` into `<group>/<slug>.md`; `compose-docs` leaves `source/` out.
